<!-- Generated from the design document, Build order tab, revision 373 (2026-11-11). Do not edit: see docs/intent/INDEX.md. -->
**Rules for the builder.**

- **One item at a time, in order.** A blocked item (the core's "Don't loop") gives way to the next that does not depend on it.
- **Branches.** Each item gets its own branch from `main`, never from another item's, with its own tests and its own report.
- **The specification** is the sections each item names, in this document and in `docs/rounds/2026-10-18-sleep-and-simulation.md` (the old round report, whose "question N" plans many items refer to). Read the rest of the document for intent only; build nothing outside the item. The document keeps changing while you work, so builders read it from its copy in the repository (archive item 10): `docs/intent/`, one file per section, cut from a stated revision of this document and refreshed after each design session. When starting an item, ask the live document for what changed since that revision; where the two differ, the live document wins. Ask again before opening the item's pull request (archive item 17), since the owner's answers to earlier items' questions often change it while it is being built: build what changed that the item touches, or, if that is large, say so in the pull request and add it to the start of the next item that touches it. A builder that cannot reach the live document, such as a session on another account, reads the copy on `main` again instead, by its diff since the item began (archive item 80; the command is in `docs/intent/INDEX.md`).
- **The design notes** (`docs/design/`, indexed by `docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md`) change in the same commit as the rule they describe, as the rulebook and the seat view do (the core's "No rule untaught").
- **Requests are rules too.** Models read their requests literally, so every field is a nudge: no field may imply something that is not true. A question about "the carried gold" when none is carried made an envoy claim gold he did not have, and an internal number ("k8") became "the peace of turn eight" sealed into a tablet. Ask only what applies, show no internal ids or numbers a king or character could repeat, and keep the engine's outcomes apart from a character's own words.
- **Balance stays frozen in every item;** item 18, the balance pass, is where the game's numbers are tuned (the core's "Numbers are first guesses until play tunes them"). Run the bot benchmarks after every item as a regression check, never to tune. A version of the rules is counted by the save version: new rules mean a new save version.
- **No rule checks which power it is** ("Different data, same rules"). Asymmetry comes from the map and starting data; only presentation and voice (season names, titles, greetings, gift lines) may name a power.
- **No model games until the build order is done.** Games with model kings or characters cost weekly usage and say little about a build that lacks the features they would test, so none are run until every item is built, and then only when the owner asks. Script games and stand-in repliers check everything until then. When model games return, every debrief, for kings and characters alike, also asks: "What did you find most and least interesting about playing this role?" A role an agent finds dull probably has too few real choices, so the answers are design data; add the question to the simulation kit's debriefs when next working on it. Each model-game report counts the mistakes of each kind that the core's "No rule untaught" sorts (archive item 205). The simulation kit's start prompt, which is what an orchestrator actually reads, points to floor rule 14 for a failed safety check.
- **Script kings and script characters are the sparring partners and the balance proxy:** strong ones give the balance pass something worth measuring (the core's "Strong computer players").
  - **Every item tests them.** After each item, play script games on its new rules, alongside the benchmarks, and look for weaknesses in the bots' play: a rule they never use, an exploit they fall for or never try, an order or errand that keeps failing, a choice a competent player would not make. While the game is incomplete a feature may not win yet, since what it needs may come in a later item (the core's "Using a feature must pay"), but every item adds its use-against-ignore numbers to one running table in the progress file, so a feature that never pays shows early, and once the game is feature complete no feature may be left whose users do not come out ahead (archive item 18). The item's report lists what was found.
  - **Every weakness found is patched** in the item at hand, for kings and characters alike, with the benchmarks recorded before and after. Once, at the start of the next item begun, audit every feature built so far the same way, and patch the gaps (as the fix pass after item 4 did for script kings never examining the inventory tablets that travel with gold).
  - **Improving their play is allowed in every item,** as an exception to frozen balance; tuning the game's own numbers still waits for item 18.
- **Progress.** The progress file keeps one line per item: its state (not started, in progress, done, blocked), its branch, its report and anything decided along the way.
- **Review points do not stop the build.** An item marked "Stop for review" is built, reviewed and merged like any other, its review questions in its report (the core's "The work never waits").
- **No stopgaps** (the core's rule), here: letters travel by themselves until item 11b, gold reaches the treasury at once until item 13, a mutinous unit disbands until bands exist; the king's tax rate comes with the hunger that answers it (item 10+a), and city-states come early (item 11+). The build order is a guide for the builders, never a rule in itself, and what counts is the final game (archive item 13): where an item's order or split serves the game badly, take the reading that builds the final game best and say so in the PR.
